name: North Lincolnshire Half Marathon & 10K
course: Single-lap, closed-road routes through countryside, starting and finishing at Quibell Park Stadium.
transport: Parking options near the village will be confirmed in the event guide.
facilities: Bag drop, toilets, chip timing; half-marathon water roughly every 5km.
rules: Half marathon minimum age 17; 10K minimum age 15. Race pack collected on the day with confirmation and photo ID.
reason: A rare single-lap countryside half with only 25m of published ascent. The on-the-day pack collection and parking guide matter for an early Scunthorpe arrival.

name: Northampton 5K, 10K & Juniors
course: Fully closed roads with a start and finish inside Sixfields Stadium.
transport: Northampton station is about a 30-minute walk; limited free stadium parking, so arrive early.
facilities: Bag drop, chip timing and event village; opens 07:30.
rules: 10K minimum age 15; 5K 11; junior race under 11. Plan around the 90-minute closure limit.
reason: The stadium finish and traffic-free course distinguish this family race. Parking is limited and the road-closure deadline may affect slower 10K runners.

name: London Half & 10K Presented by TREK
place: London Stadium, Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park
course: East London course based at the London Stadium and Olympic Park; consult the distance-specific route map.
transport: Use public transport for the Olympic Park; confirm the stadium entry gate in the final guide.
facilities: Bag drop, chip-timed results and finish-line refreshments.
rules: The organiser page's title mentions March but the listed event date is 28 February 2027; confirm before travel.
reason: A stadium-based winter half with a 38-minute gap before the 10K starts. The organiser's inconsistent month wording makes a pre-travel date check sensible.

name: Regent's Park 5K & 10K April
place: The Broad Walk, Regent's Park, London
course: Flat park course on tarmac paths; check lap count and separation point for your distance.
transport: Regent's Park, Great Portland Street and Baker Street stations are nearby; no dedicated event parking.
facilities: Bag drop, park toilets, chip timing and finish refreshments.
rules: Contact the organiser in advance if you expect to exceed the published cut-off guidance.
reason: A flat city-centre park race with simultaneous starts. Public transport is the straightforward choice because dedicated race parking is absent.

name: Twycross Zoo 10K
course: First and final sections inside the zoo, with the middle of the route on closed roads.
transport: Free on-site parking; organiser advises arriving before 08:00 to avoid queues.
facilities: Bag drop, portable toilets, water at 5km and finish; race entry includes post-race zoo entry.
rules: Spectator ticket details are pending; check them before planning a family visit.
reason: The included zoo entry can turn this into a full-day outing. Early pack collection and parking queues are key to making the 09:00 start.

name: Peterborough Running Festival
course: Marked park routes with distance-specific splits through Nene Park.
transport: Paid parking at Nene Park or Ferry Meadows, about two minutes from the event village.
facilities: Bag drop, visitor-centre toilets, water every 5km on longer distances.
rules: Minimum ages: half 17, 10K 15, 5K 11. Follow signs where distances diverge and rejoin.
reason: A near-flat half in a large green space, with shorter options. The route splits and 12:30 scheduled end are useful for pacing and meeting supporters.

name: Hemel Hempstead 5K & 10K
start: 5K 09:00; 10K listed as 09:10 at top and 09:08 in schedule—confirm final time.
course: Undulating closed-road town-centre and High Street route; 5K map shows 64m ascent.
transport: Hemel Hempstead station is about a 20-minute walk; no event parking, paid town car parks available.
facilities: Bag drop, portable toilets, water around 2km on both routes and 7km on 10K.
rules: The page states minimum age 15 without separating distances; verify 5K eligibility. Wheelchair and buggy runners welcome; no dogs.
reason: A useful town-centre option with an undulating profile rather than a flat PB course. The published 10K start time conflicts by two minutes, so check the final guide.

name: Run Redditch Half Marathon & 10K
course: Routes based at Arrow Valley Country Park; use the organiser's distance map for surface and lap details.
transport: Confirm the race-day park entrance and parking area in the final event guide.
facilities: Bag drop, chip timing and event village with finish refreshments.
rules: Junior event has a separate late-morning start; check its age and supervision conditions before entry.
reason: The 10K and half start only five minutes apart, while juniors go at 11:30. Families can plan around those gaps and the park meeting point.
